_comment: `gateFiles` is a TIGHTENING: it names the files where a forbidden pattern
means a defeated gate rather than ordinary code, so no ledger entry can
excuse one. scripts/ci/** is this repository's pipeline - local-ci.mjs,
secret-scan.mjs, docker-gate.mjs, sast-gate.mjs and the ratchet all DEFINE
gates, so a `|| true` or a `--no-verify` in any of them is exactly the
class the doctrine refuses to let anyone write down and move on from.
.husky/** is where those gates are bound to git.
`exclude` is deliberately EMPTY and should stay that way. An operator-added
exclude applies only to ledgerable rules (it can never hide a forbidden
marker), and every glob added here becomes a SCAN-EXCLUDE marker that needs
its own dated ledger entry pinned to that exact glob - because one line of
config would otherwise void the whole scan with nothing to review.
